newsitem.title: USA: Toshiba Corp unveils 2-pound notebook PC.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba Corp unveils 2-pound notebook PC.

text.p: Toshiba Corp. on Monday launched a new line of lightweight "mini-notebook" computers, including a model that weighs less than 2 pounds.
The world's leading notebook PC maker said its new Libretto line is intended to be a companion to full-size desktop computers and to be used for mobile communications and information management.
Toshiba said the Libretto 50CT is the first full-function notebook that weighs less than 2 pounds and runs Microsoft Corp.'s Windows 95 operating system. It has a list price of $1,999.
Toshiba made the announcement at Spring Comdex/Spring'97, a major computer trade show under way this week in Atlanta.

The Tokyo-based company also unveiled the newest members of its Satellite notebook family, the 220 CDS and 225 CDS, which are aimed at the corporate and consumer markets respectively. Both computers also are priced at $1,999.
In 1996, Toshiba said it held roughly half the U.S. market for portable computers priced under $1,999, citing data from market research firm Audits & Surveys.
Other new machines unveiled by Toshiba include the Portege 300, with a suggested list price of $3,499, and the Satellite Pro 440 Series, starting in the mid-$2,000 range.
Overall, Toshiba remains the top supplier of portable computers, with a 24.4 percent share of the U.S. market in the first quarter of 1997, according to International Data Corp.
